subject: Re: SLA template — availability margin exception & monthly credit worksheet
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@apexanalytics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA request — monthly availability margin & credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here — we have a couple of asks on Redwood's standard SLA template before legal will greenlight the PO. Attached is a redline of the template plus a short worksheet of our expected monthly usage. The two items specific to discuss:

- Availability floor: we need assurance of 99.95% across primary region with a carveout for scheduled maintenance limited to 6 hours/month.
- Monthly credit caps: given our spend profile, we require a clearer remediation ladder (credits per % below) and a hard cap per month.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Offer a 99.95% baseline (instead of standard 99.9%) for this enterprise tier?
2) Provide the proposed ladder in the attached worksheet or suggest an alternate (we are OK with staged credits but want predictable P&L impact).

If helpful we can hop on a call — procurement + finance — to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Maria Torres
Head of Procurement
Apex Analytics

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: draft credit ladder for Apex — see worksheet

Rishi / Markus —

I reviewed Maria's worksheet and modeled three ladder options in the attached XLSX: Conservative, Balanced, and Aggressive. Key assumptions:

- Baseline availability target set to 99.95% (per request).
- Monthly credit tiers (example, Balanced):
  * 99.95%–99.90%: 10% of monthly invoice
  * 99.90%–99.50%: 25% of monthly invoice
  * <99.50%: 50% of monthly invoice, capped at 100% of that month's invoice
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance <= 6 hours/month excluded if notified 72 hours in advance. Emergency maintenance will be handled case-by-case and not count toward credits unless caused by Redwood platform failure.
- Hard cap: propose 100% of monthly invoice as absolute cap (we can discuss escrow structures if they want additional protection).

Tradeoffs: Conservative keeps our downside limited (smaller credits, higher cap), Aggressive matches their ask but increases our financial exposure. Balanced is a middle ground and is usually acceptable to procurement.

I recommend we share the Balanced worksheet in the call and offer the Conservative ladder only if they push back on the cap.

Monica
Director, Customer Reliability & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-credit-worksheet-20270916.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@apexanalytics.com>, procurement@apexanalytics.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: 99.95% baseline + proposed credit ladder

Maria — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we've drafted a proposal that maps to your worksheet while keeping a clear liability cap. High level:

- Availability commitment: 99.95% in primary region for the Dedicated Enterprise tier.
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours/month excluded if Redwood provides >=72 hours notice. Unscheduled emergency maintenance (platform-driven) will be evaluated and, if found to be Redwood-caused, included in the availability calculation.
- Proposed credit ladder (Balanced):
  * Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.90%–99.949%: 10% credit of that month's invoice
  * 99.50%–99.899%: 25% credit of that month's invoice
  * <99.50%: 50% credit of that month's invoice, with hard cap at 100% of that month's invoice

We attach the worksheet for review ("proposed-credit-worksheet-20270916.xlsx") and a redline of the SLA template in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/SLAs/RW-2027-0412.

If those terms look acceptable we can:
1) Have legal align final language (I can introduce our contracts counsel).
2) Execute via DocuSign and move forward with the SOW and PO.

Call suggestion: Mon 9/20 10am PT to finalize commercials and agree on signature path. Does that work for your team?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
